text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
MakeWeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
InviteOthers(x) ::: x invites others to come to their ceremony.
WellAttended(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
InviteFriends(x) ::: x invites friends to their ceremony.
Premises:
∀x (MakeWeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are people who are engaged.
∀x (InviteOthers(x) → MakeWeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others to come to their ceremony make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttended(x) → InviteOthers(x)) ::: Anyone who has a well-attended wedding invites others to come to their ceremony.
∃x (WellAttended(x) ∧ LargerFamily(x)) ::: Some people that have well-attended weddings have larger families.
(Engaged(john) → ¬(InviteFriends(john) ∧ MakeWeddingPlans(john))) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends to their ceremony and make wedding plans.
(LargerFamily(john) → (WellAttended(john) ∨ InviteFriends(john))) ::: If John has a larger family, then either John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends to their ceremony.
Conclusion:
Engaged(john) ::: John is engaged.
